1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-command-deck
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The Command Deck is the customer-facing front end of the Daliesk agent enterprise: 147 defined agents, the workflows between them, the live activity of a harness run, and a code-safety review placed on the target repository's own code.
6	
7	It is a Next.js 14 application (App Router, React 18) whose three scenes are three.js through `@react-three/fiber`. It reads one HTTP feed and, when that feed does not answer, replays the fixtures committed beside it — so the deck is fully usable, and demonstrable, with no server running and no API key.
8	
9	## Run it
10	
11	Run the first from the repository root; the second is `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck dev` under another name.
12	
13	```sh
14	pnpm install
15	pnpm run deck
16	```
17	
18	The deck serves on `http://localhost:3000`. Point it at a live feed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL`; the default is `http://localhost:4711`.
19	
20	The second line is the production build and the server over it; the third snapshots `fixtures/` from a running feed.
21	
22	```sh
23	NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL=http://localhost:4711 pnpm run deck
24	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build && pnpm --dir apps/command-deck start
25	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures
26	```
27	
28	## The three views
29	
30	| Key | View | What it shows |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `1` | **Enterprise** (`/`) | Every defined agent as a node, clustered by division inside a soft nebula in the division's colour; edges are the delegations, verifications and judgements between them. Traffic runs along an edge only while one of its two agents has acted in the last few seconds, coloured by the relationship's kind; with nothing live the edges only breathe. An agent at work wears a turning orbital ring, a certified agent a warm rim, a failed one a dim red rim, and a certificate lands as an expanding ring with a short beam of light. Clicking a node flies the camera to it, dims everything unrelated, and opens its role, model route, preset, skills, tools, source file and its own events in the run being followed; `Esc` flies back. |
33	| `2` | **Process** (`/process`) | The program pipeline as a lit corridor: each department lane is a glowing rail in its division's colour, running from the left edge through three tall glass gates, Verification, Judging and Integration, over a floor grid that recedes into the fog. Every logged event travels its lane as a comet with a ribbon trail, sized and coloured by kind; a certificate rings the Verification gate, a merge lights Integration and leaves it lit. A lane's label names the agent working it and its event count, and brightens while that agent is acting. The camera opens on an establishing move, drifts while the run produces, and pulls back to frame every lane once the run has ended. A timeline scrubber drags a time plane along the pipeline; `Head` returns to live. |
34	| `3` | **Code safety** (`/safety`) | The reviewed repository as a code city at night: directories are districts, each floor outlined in the colour of the language most of it is written in, and files are blocks scaled by size whose windows are lit in proportion to the file's bytes, keyed on the path so one file lights the same windows in every render. Every finding stands a shaft of light on the roof of its file, tallest and brightest for critical and shortest for info, with a breathing halo at its foot; hovering one names the file, the line and the finding, and selecting one flies the camera onto its building and hangs a callout on the shaft. While any department of the loaded review is still pending, a wall of light sweeps the city every few seconds and the district outlines pulse with it; the sweep stops when the last department releases. The panel holds the findings table with severity, department and CWE filters, the certificate with its counts and its unverified list, the bilingual report, downloads, and the form that starts a new review. |
35	
36	`Esc` clears the selection and flies each stage back: the enterprise view to the whole graph, the code city to its resting height. The enterprise view opens on an establishing shot, the camera easing in from far out and high above the graph over two and a half seconds; the code city opens on a three-second fly-over from high over its far edge. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` opens every view at rest, stops the traffic, the auto-orbit, the pulsing and the chromatic aberration, holds bloom at a constant intensity, and cuts to a selected agent instead of flying; in the process view it holds the camera at one angle over the whole pipeline and stands each event as a still dot on its own rail; in the code city it skips the fly-over, cuts to a selected finding, holds the scan line still at the centre and stops the windows and the halos breathing.
37	
38	`F` gives the stage the whole frame: the side panel hides and the header keeps only the mark, the counts and the live badge. `P` starts a tour that walks the three views every thirty seconds, opening each with a title card whose two lines are composed from what the deck has read: the agent and relationship counts, the run and its event count, the reviewed target with its findings and whether it is certified. Any key or click ends the tour. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the kinetic title, the route dissolve and the counter tweens are also off; every mode still works.
39	
40	![The enterprise view: 147 agents in ten division clusters](docs/enterprise.png)
41	
42	![The process view: departments, verification, judging and integration](docs/process.png)
43	
44	![The code-safety view: the code city with findings on their files](docs/safety.png)
45	
46	## The feed contract
47	
48	The deck reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` (default `http://localhost:4711`) and expects these paths. The feed server itself is not in this package.
49	
50	| Path | Answer |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| `GET /roster` | `{ generatedAt, counts: { defined, active }, divisions[], agents[], edges[] }` — the 147 agents, their divisions and their relationships. |
53	| `GET /runs` | `[{ id, kind, name, startedAt, endedAt?, status, path }]` for every `program`, `fleet`, `experiment` and `code-safety` run. |
54	| `GET /runs/:id/events` | Server-Sent Events. Each `data:` frame is one `{ ts, seq, agentId, sessionId, kind, label, detail?, severity?, file?, line? }`. The stream replays history and then stays open. |
55	| `GET /safety/:id` | `{ target, departments, findings, certificate, report }` for one code-safety review. |
56	| `POST /safety` | `{ target, model? }` starts a review and answers `{ id }`; the deck then follows that run live. `target` is an absolute path on the feed's machine and `model` is `sonnet` or `opus`, the names `pnpm run code-safety -- --model` accepts; the form opens on the loaded review's own target. |
57	
58	Every field is typed in [`deck/contract.ts`](deck/contract.ts), which is the one place the contract is written down. `seq` is what the client deduplicates on, so a reconnection that replays history delivers nothing twice. The footer's events per minute is counted from the `ts` of the frames in the event window over the last sixty seconds: a live feed measures that minute against the wall clock, so a feed that stops reporting decays to `—`; replay measures it against the newest recorded frame, because fixture timestamps are historical. Nothing is extrapolated.
59	
60	Two deck-side rules are worth knowing because the feed does not carry them. A finding's owning department is derived from its CWE through the table in [`deck/departments.ts`](deck/departments.ts), since the feed reports per-department totals but places no department on the finding itself. A finding counts as verified unless the certificate's `unverified` list names it.
61	
62	## Replay: what happens with no feed
63	
64	On load the deck sends one `GET /roster` to the configured feed with a 5-second timeout. Any failure — connection refused, timeout, non-2xx, a blocked cross-origin request — selects replay mode, and every later read goes to the deck's own routes under `/api/fixtures`, which serve the same paths with the same payloads. The header badge reads `REPLAY` instead of `LIVE`, the status footer names the feed it could not reach, and each view carries a standing **Example data** notice, so a screenshot cannot be mistaken for a live run.
65	
66	The replayed event stream is paced rather than dumped: the route delivers the first 60% of the recording immediately as history, then releases the rest a frame at a time, then holds the connection open. A keyless demo therefore shows an enterprise at work rather than a static file.
67	
68	`POST /safety` in replay mode reopens the recorded review instead of starting a new one, and says so under the form.
69	
70	## The fixtures
71	
72	`fixtures/` is a snapshot of the real feed, taken by `scripts/snapshot-fixtures.ts` (`pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures` with `pnpm run feed` running): nothing in it is invented, and the script refuses a live run directory because only committed records have their key material redacted.
73	
74	- `fixtures/roster.json` — the feed's `GET /roster`: the generated [`data/enterprise/roster.json`](../../data/enterprise/README.md), 147 agents in ten divisions and 124 relationships, with the statuses the recorded runs gave them.
75	- `fixtures/runs.json` — five committed records: the two code-safety reviews recorded on 2026-09-19 (the second NodeGoat run, the Java dvja run), a tier-5 fleet, a paired experiment, and the csv-tools program.
76	- `fixtures/events/<run>.jsonl` — each record's session logs folded by the feed into the event stream the deck follows: 1,079 events for the NodeGoat review, from the departments' opening directives through their tool calls to the four certificates and the two merges.
77	- `fixtures/safety/<run>.json` — the feed's `GET /safety/:id` for each review: the NodeGoat review's 111 files and 38 verified findings, the dvja review's 174 files and 40, each with its departments, its certificate and its bilingual report.
78	
79	The recorded reviews are the same ones [`data/code-safety/README.md`](../../data/code-safety/README.md) reads recall against, so a replay shows exactly what the live run showed.
80	
81	## Layout
82	
83	| Directory | Holds |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| `app/` | The routes, and the fixture endpoints under `app/api/fixtures/`. |
86	| `components/` | The shell, and one folder per view; everything touching three.js is a Client Component. |
87	| `deck/` | The contract, the feed client, the event stream, the store, the layouts, the palette. |
88	| `fixtures/` | The committed replay data. |
89	| `scripts/` | The fixture snapshot script. |
90	| `docs/` | The screenshots above. |
91	
92	The shell (`app/layout.tsx`) is a Server Component. Each scene is loaded through `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, because three.js reaches for a WebGL context on mount.
93	
94	## Limitations
95	
96	A run's recorded history reaches the deck in one burst, so the process view releases its comets from a queue at a fixed rate: every logged event is seen to travel, a few seconds after the panel has already counted it.
97	
98	The deck reads; it never writes to a repository and never runs a review itself — `POST /safety` asks the feed to. A live feed on another origin must send CORS headers the browser accepts, or the deck falls back to replay. The scenes need WebGL 2; there is no 2D fallback. The code city places a finding only when the target's file list contains its `file`, and a finding on a file the feed did not report is listed in the table but stands no beacon. At the widest zoom the shared bloom catches the lit windows themselves and softens the city slightly; the grade is one composer for the three views, tuned for the beams and the rails first.
99

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities

1	/**
2	 * The deck's single client store.
3	 *
4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity` and `bursts` — is mutated in
6	 * place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second render pass
7	 * must not go through React at all.
8	 */
9	
10	'use client'
11	
12	import { create } from 'zustand'
13	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
14	import { getRoster, getRuns, getSafety, resolveFeed, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
15	import { subscribeRun, type StreamState } from './stream.ts'
16	
17	/** How many events one run keeps in memory; older frames fall off the head. */
18	const EVENT_WINDOW = 4_000
19	
20	/** How often a live deck re-reads the run list and a running review's detail. */
21	const REFRESH_MS = 10_000
22	
23	/** A certificate burst waiting to be drawn once, then dropped. */
24	interface Burst {
25	  agentId: string
26	  at: number
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * How the deck is being shown.
31	 *
32	 * `off` is the working deck: header, stage and panel. `focus` hides the panel
33	 * and gives the stage the whole frame. `tour` is `focus` plus a timer that
34	 * walks the three views, announcing each one; anything the viewer does ends it.
35	 */
36	type PresentationMode = 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour'
37	
38	/** Everything the deck holds for one session. */
39	export interface DeckState {
40	  source: FeedSource | undefined
41	  streamState: StreamState
42	  roster: Roster | undefined
43	  runs: Run[]
44	  selectedRunId: string | undefined
45	  events: RunEvent[]
46	  safety: SafetyReview | undefined
47	  safetyRunId: string | undefined
48	  selectedAgentId: string | undefined
49	  selectedFindingId: string | undefined
50	  error: string | undefined
51	  booted: boolean
52	  /** Timeline position as a sequence number; `undefined` follows the head. */
53	  cursor: number | undefined
54	  /** Last activity timestamp per agent, in `performance.now()` milliseconds. */
55	  activity: Map<string, number>
56	  /** Certificate bursts the enterprise scene has not drawn yet. */
57	  bursts: Burst[]
58	  /** How the deck is being shown; presentation only, no effect on what is read. */
59	  presentation: PresentationMode
60	  boot: () => Promise<void>
61	  selectRun: (id: string) => void
62	  /** List a run the feed does not report yet, such as a review this deck just started. */
63	  addRun: (run: Run) => void
64	  /** Re-read the run list and, while the followed review is still running, its detail. */
65	  refresh: () => Promise<void>
66	  selectAgent: (id: string | undefined) => void
67	  selectFinding: (id: string | undefined) => void
68	  setCursor: (seq: number | undefined) => void
69	  /** Load a review's detail; `force` re-reads one already loaded. */
70	  loadSafety: (id: string, force?: boolean) => Promise<void>
71	  setPresentation: (mode: PresentationMode) => void
72	  /** Enter one presentation mode, or leave it when it is already the current one. */
73	  togglePresentation: (mode: Exclude<PresentationMode, 'off'>) => void
74	}
75	
76	let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined
77	
78	/**
79	 * Append one event to the window, dropping the oldest frames past the cap.
80	 * @param events - The current window.
81	 * @param event - The frame to append.
82	 * @returns The new window.
83	 */
84	function appendEvent(events: RunEvent[], event: RunEvent): RunEvent[] {
85	  const next = [...events, event]
86	  return next.length > EVENT_WINDOW ? next.slice(next.length - EVENT_WINDOW) : next
87	}
88	
89	export const useDeck = create<DeckState>((set, get) => ({
90	  source: undefined,
91	  streamState: 'idle',
92	  roster: undefined,
93	  runs: [],
94	  selectedRunId: undefined,
95	  events: [],
96	  safety: undefined,
97	  safetyRunId: undefined,
98	  selectedAgentId: undefined,
99	  selectedFindingId: undefined,
100	  error: undefined,
101	  booted: false,
102	  cursor: undefined,
103	  activity: new Map<string, number>(),
104	  bursts: [],
105	  presentation: 'off',
106	
107	  boot: async () => {
108	    if (get().booted) return
109	    set({ booted: true })
110	    const source = await resolveFeed()
111	    set({ source })
112	    try {
113	      const [roster, runs] = await Promise.all([getRoster(source.base), getRuns(source.base)])
114	      set({ roster, runs })
115	      const safetyRun = runs.find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety') ?? runs[0]
116	      if (safetyRun !== undefined) get().selectRun(safetyRun.id)
117	    } catch (error) {
118	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
119	    }
120	    // Replay is a fixed record; only a live feed changes underneath the deck.
121	    if (source.mode === 'live') setInterval(() => { void get().refresh() }, REFRESH_MS)
122	  },
123	
124	  addRun: (run) => {
125	    set(state => (state.runs.some(entry => entry.id === run.id) ? {} : { runs: [run, ...state.runs] }))
126	  },
127	
128	  refresh: async () => {
129	    const { source, runs: known, selectedRunId } = get()
130	    if (source === undefined) return
131	    try {
132	      const listed = await getRuns(source.base)
133	      // A review this deck started stays listed until the feed reports it.
134	      const pending = known.filter(run => !listed.some(entry => entry.id === run.id))
135	      set({ runs: [...pending, ...listed] })
136	      const selected = [...pending, ...listed].find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)
137	      if (selected?.kind === 'code-safety' && (selected.status === 'running' || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id)) {
138	        await get().loadSafety(selected.id, true)
139	      }
140	    } catch (error) {
141	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
142	    }
143	  },
144	
145	  selectRun: (id) => {
146	    const source = get().source
147	    if (source === undefined || get().selectedRunId === id) return
148	    unsubscribe?.()
149	    set({ selectedRunId: id, events: [], cursor: undefined })
150	    const { activity, bursts } = get()
151	    activity.clear()
152	    // A certificate queued under the previous run must not burst on this one.
153	    bursts.length = 0
154	    unsubscribe = subscribeRun(source.base, id, {
155	      onState: state => set({ streamState: state }),
156	      onEvent: (event) => {
157	        get().activity.set(event.agentId, performance.now())
158	        if (event.kind === 'certificate') {
159	          get().bursts.push({ agentId: event.agentId, at: performance.now() })
160	        }
161	        set(state => ({ events: appendEvent(state.events, event) }))
162	      },
163	    })
164	    const run = get().runs.find(entry => entry.id === id)
165	    if (run?.kind === 'code-safety') void get().loadSafety(id)
166	  },
167	
168	  selectAgent: id => set({ selectedAgentId: id }),
169	  selectFinding: id => set({ selectedFindingId: id }),
170	  setCursor: seq => set({ cursor: seq }),
171	
172	  loadSafety: async (id, force = false) => {
173	    const source = get().source
174	    if (source === undefined || (!force && get().safetyRunId === id)) return
175	    try {
176	      // No finding is preselected: the view opens on the whole city, and the
177	      // camera only flies in once a reviewer picks one. A re-read keeps the
178	      // selection when the finding is still there.
179	      const safety = await getSafety(source.base, id)
180	      const selectedFindingId = get().selectedFindingId
181	      const kept = force && safety.findings.some(finding => finding.id === selectedFindingId) ? selectedFindingId : undefined
182	      set({ safety, safetyRunId: id, selectedFindingId: kept, error: undefined })
183	    } catch (error) {
184	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
185	    }
186	  },
187	
188	  setPresentation: mode => set({ presentation: mode }),
189	  togglePresentation: mode => set(state => ({
190	    presentation: state.presentation === mode ? 'off' : mode,
191	  })),
192	}))
193	
194	/**
195	 * The events the timeline currently admits.
196	 * @param events - The full window.
197	 * @param cursor - Sequence cap, or `undefined` to follow the head.
198	 * @returns Events up to and including the cursor.
199	 */
200	export function eventsUpTo(events: readonly RunEvent[], cursor: number | undefined): RunEvent[] {
201	  if (cursor === undefined) return [...events]
202	  return events.filter(event => event.seq <= cursor)
203	}

1	/**
2	 * The code city's layout.
3	 *
4	 * Directories become districts on a grid, files become blocks inside their
5	 * district. Block footprint is constant and height carries size, so a large
6	 * file reads as a tower rather than as a sprawl — which keeps the finding
7	 * beacons above each block separable at a glance.
8	 *
9	 * The layout also carries the two values the night-city material needs per
10	 * building: the fraction of its windows that are lit, which rises with file
11	 * size, and a window-pattern seed derived from the file path, so one file
12	 * lights the same windows in every render and in every session.
13	 */
14	
15	import type { SafetyTarget, TargetFile } from './contract.ts'
16	
17	/** One file, placed. */
18	export interface CityBlock {
19	  path: string
20	  language: string
21	  bytes: number
22	  x: number
23	  z: number
24	  /** Block height in scene units. */
25	  height: number
26	  /** Square footprint side in scene units. */
27	  size: number
28	  /** Position in `CityLayout.blocks`, which is the instance order of the building mesh. */
29	  index: number
30	  /** Directory this block stands in, as `CityDistrict.path` names it. */
31	  district: string
32	  /** Fraction of the building's windows that are lit, rising with file size. */
33	  lit: number
34	  /** Window-pattern seed in `[0, 1)`, derived from the file path. */
35	  seed: number
36	}
37	
38	/** One directory, placed, with the plate under its blocks. */
39	interface CityDistrict {
40	  path: string
41	  x: number
42	  z: number
43	  width: number
44	  depth: number
45	  blocks: CityBlock[]
46	  /** The language most of the district's files are written in; it colours the district outline. */
47	  language: string
48	}
49	
50	/** The laid-out city. */
51	export interface CityLayout {
52	  districts: CityDistrict[]
53	  /** Every block in one flat list; the order is the building mesh's instance order. */
54	  blocks: CityBlock[]
55	  /** Every block by path, for finding placement and selection. */
56	  byPath: Map<string, CityBlock>
57	  /** Half-extent of the city footprint, for camera framing. */
58	  extent: number
59	}
60	
61	/** Footprint of one file block. */
62	const BLOCK = 3.2
63	
64	/** Gap between blocks inside a district. */
65	const BLOCK_GAP = 1.5
66	
67	/** Gap between districts. */
68	const DISTRICT_GAP = 6
69	
70	/** Height of the smallest block, so an empty file is still visible. */
71	const MIN_HEIGHT = 1.4
72	
73	/** Height of the largest block; every other height scales between the two. */
74	const MAX_HEIGHT = 17
75	
76	/** Lit-window fraction of the smallest file. */
77	const MIN_LIT = 0.08
78	
79	/** Lit-window fraction of the largest file. */
80	const MAX_LIT = 0.44
81	
82	/**
83	 * Directory of one repository-relative path.
84	 * @param path - Repository-relative file path.
85	 * @returns The directory, or `/` for a file at the repository root.
86	 */
87	function directoryOf(path: string): string {
88	  const cut = path.lastIndexOf('/')
89	  return cut === -1 ? '/' : path.slice(0, cut)
90	}
91	
92	/**
93	 * The window-pattern seed of one file, as an FNV-1a hash folded into `[0, 1)`.
94	 * @param path - Repository-relative file path.
95	 * @returns A stable seed for that path.
96	 */
97	function seedOf(path: string): number {
98	  let hash = 2_166_136_261
99	  for (let index = 0; index < path.length; index += 1) {
100	    hash ^= path.charCodeAt(index)
101	    hash = Math.imul(hash, 16_777_619)
102	  }
103	  return ((hash >>> 0) % 4_096) / 4_096
104	}
105	
106	/**
107	 * The language most of a district's files are written in.
108	 * @param files - The district's files.
109	 * @returns The most frequent language, ties broken by name.
110	 */
111	function dominantLanguage(files: readonly TargetFile[]): string {
112	  const counts = new Map<string, number>()
113	  for (const file of files) counts.set(file.language, (counts.get(file.language) ?? 0) + 1)
114	  return [...counts.entries()]
115	    .sort((left, right) => (right[1] - left[1]) || left[0].localeCompare(right[0]))[0]?.[0] ?? 'Other'
116	}
117	
118	/**
119	 * Lay out the reviewed repository as a city.
120	 * @param target - The target the feed reported.
121	 * @returns Districts, the flat block list, the path index, and the footprint extent.
122	 */
123	export function layoutCity(target: SafetyTarget): CityLayout {
124	  const groups = new Map<string, TargetFile[]>()
125	  for (const file of target.files) {
126	    const directory = directoryOf(file.path)
127	    const list = groups.get(directory) ?? []
128	    list.push(file)
129	    groups.set(directory, list)
130	  }
131	
132	  const largest = target.files.reduce((acc, file) => Math.max(acc, file.bytes), 1)
133	  const ordered = [...groups.entries()].sort((left, right) => left[0].localeCompare(right[0]))
134	
135	  // Districts are laid on a near-square grid, widest first along each row.
136	  const columns = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(ordered.length)))
137	  const districts: CityDistrict[] = []
138	  const blocks: CityBlock[] = []
139	  const byPath = new Map<string, CityBlock>()
140	
141	  const sized = ordered.map(([path, files]) => {
142	    const side = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(files.length)))
143	    const width = (side * BLOCK) + ((side - 1) * BLOCK_GAP) + 3
144	    return { path, files, side, width }
145	  })

# Agent Note: The Command Deck reads one feed and replays committed fixtures when it does not answer

Status: implemented

English | [中文](2026-09-19-command-deck.zh.md)

## Problem

A customer proof of concept has to show the Daliesk enterprise working — 147 defined agents, the workflows between them, live activity from harness runs, and a code-safety review placed on a target repository's code — on a laptop, in a meeting room, tomorrow. The repository could show the same facts as logs and generated catalogues, but a room full of executives reads a scene, not a JSONL file. Nothing in the repository rendered an agent roster, a program pipeline, or a code-safety result at all.

Three constraints shaped the design and pull against each other. The feed server that supplies this data is written by a different agent, in parallel, so the front end could not wait for it and could not discover its behaviour by running it. The demo must survive a room with no network and no API key, because a proof of concept that shows an empty screen is worse than no proof of concept. And nothing on screen may be mistaken for a live result when it is not, because a claim a client repeats is a claim the repository has to stand behind.

## Decision

**One contract file, two sources behind it.** `deck/contract.ts` is the only place the feed's paths and payloads are written down. `resolveFeed()` sends one `GET /roster` to `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` with a 5-second timeout (a cold feed folds every recorded session before its first answer) and returns a base URL: the configured feed when it answers, and the deck's own `/api/fixtures` routes otherwise. Those routes serve the same paths with the same payloads, so every reader downstream — the store, the three scenes, the panels — is written once against one contract and never learns which source it is reading. A failed probe is not an error state to recover from; it is the other half of a two-valued choice the status bar reports.

**Replay is paced, not dumped.** The fixture event route delivers the first 60% of a recording immediately as history, then releases the rest a frame at a time, then holds the connection open with heartbeats — the behaviour the live endpoint's own contract describes. Interleaving the recorded phases (department sweeps, findings, the verifier's re-read, judging, integration) rather than laying them down in sequence is what keeps all four pipeline stages populated from the opening seconds. A keyless demo therefore shows an enterprise at work.

**Example data says so, on every view.** In replay mode the header badge reads `REPLAY`, the status footer names the feed it could not reach, and each view carries a standing notice. The notice sits inside the panel rather than once in the shell so that a screenshot of any single view carries the claim with it.

**The fixtures are a snapshot of the feed, never generated.** `scripts/snapshot-fixtures.ts` writes `fixtures/` from a running feed: the generated roster, five committed records under `data/`, their session logs folded into event streams, and the two code-safety reviews' details. It refuses a run directory outside `data/` because only committed records have their key material redacted. Every finding replay shows is one a department wrote and the committed examiner re-read at its line, at a named revision. A fabricated finding on a real, well-known target is the one thing in this demo a security-literate reader could catch, and the repository's own records make it unnecessary.

**Frame state never goes through React.** The store keeps `activity` and `bursts` as objects mutated in place and read from `useFrame`; only roster, runs, events and selection are React state. Each scene draws in a handful of calls — instanced meshes for nodes, file blocks and beacons, one additive point layer per glow, one line-segment layer per edge set — so 147 agents, 124 curved edges with their traffic, a pipeline of comets and a lit code city with a beacon per finding leave the frame budget to the grade.

**One grade, three choreographed stages, one keyboard.** `components/three/Stage.tsx` is the single canvas every view renders through: bloom, ACES tone mapping as its own effect (the composer forces `NoToneMapping` on the renderer), film grain and a vignette in one pass, then chromatic aberration, then SMAA on the graded image, over a shared atmosphere of dust and horizon glow. Each stage owns its choreography and nothing else: the enterprise opens on an establishing shot, runs traffic along an edge only while one of its agents has just acted, and flies to a selected node; the process pipeline releases every logged event as a comet from a queue at a fixed rate through the Verification, Judging and Integration gates, so recorded history that arrives in one burst is still seen to travel; the code city lights a window grid keyed on each file's path and size, stands a beacon per finding sized by severity, sweeps a wall of light while a department is pending, and flies onto a selected finding. `F` hides the panel and `P` walks the three views every thirty seconds behind a title card composed from what the deck has read; any key or click ends the tour. The shell's one keyboard handler in `components/shell/usePresentation.ts` owns every shortcut, so `Esc` clears the selected agent and the selected finding wherever it is pressed and no stage listens for keys itself.

**The deck is a standalone Next.js program.** Its `tsconfig.json` is its own; it joins neither the host nor the client project-reference aggregate, because it is a browser application built by `next build` rather than a package the repository's `tsc -b` emits.

## Consequences

`pnpm run deck` and `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build` work from a clean checkout with no key and no feed, and `pnpm run poc` builds the deck, starts the feed and serves the production build in one command for the demonstration machine. Because `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures` is a snapshot, replay shows what the recorded runs showed and a reviewer can diff `fixtures/` against `data/code-safety`; refreshing the fixtures after a new record is one command, not a generator edit.

Two facts the feed does not carry are derived deck-side and documented as such in the README: a finding's owning department, from its CWE through the table in `deck/departments.ts`, and its verification state, from whether the certificate's `unverified` list names it. If the feed later places a department on the finding, that table becomes dead code and should go.

`pnpm run constraints` reports four violations for this package that cannot be fixed from inside it. `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts` treats every `apps/*` directory as a release member — it must not be `private`, it must set `publishConfig.access`, its repository field must name its directory, and its name must appear in that script's `appPackageFiles` policy. A customer proof of concept is not a published package, so the manifest stays `private: true` and the gate stays red until the script grows a case for an app that is not published.

The scenes need WebGL 2 and have no 2D fallback. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` opens every stage at rest, cuts to a selection instead of flying, stands each process event as a still dot, holds the city's scan line still, and stops the traffic, the breathing, the pulsing and the chromatic aberration, which is the accessibility floor, not a full alternative rendering. The grade is the dominant frame cost. Measured under software rendering on this host, the shell's post stack costs about 1.4× the frame before it, almost all of it SMAA; the enterprise stage costs 1.15× its predecessor; the code city costs 0.96× because severity and selection moved from a per-frame typed-array rewrite into instanced attributes updated on change. The shared bloom threshold also catches the lit windows at the widest zoom, which softens the city slightly. Bloom and device pixel ratio are the two knobs to turn first on a weak GPU.

## Alternatives considered

- **Wait for the feed server, then build against it.** The two halves are written in parallel against one written contract precisely so neither blocks the other; a front end that cannot start without its server also cannot demo without it.
- **Bundle the fixtures as imported JSON.** Simpler, and it would lose the thing that makes the replay convincing: a paced Server-Sent Events stream with reconnection, exercised by the same client code the live feed drives. Files on disk also stay reviewable as data.
- **A separate "demo mode" switch.** Two code paths through every view, one of which is only ever exercised in a meeting room. The fallback is instead a base URL, so the demo path is the production path.
- **Invent the code-safety findings.** Faster to write and indefensible in the room. The repository's own recorded reviews already place real findings on their lines at a named revision.
- **A 2D graph (SVG or canvas) for the enterprise.** It would carry the roster and the edges, and none of the reason a client believes the enterprise is real. The 3D scene is the deliverable, not decoration.
- **A grade per stage.** Each scene tuning its own bloom would let the code city sharpen its windows without dimming the enterprise beams, at the price of three grades that drift apart. The one shared composer is what makes the three scenes read as one instrument; a stage that needs a different look changes its materials.

3	import { usePathname, useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
4	import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
5	import { useDeck } from '@/deck/store'
6	import { VIEWS } from './views.ts'
7	
8	/** How long the tour holds one view before moving to the next. */
9	const TOUR_STEP_MS = 30_000
10	
11	/** Elements that own their own keystrokes, where the deck's shortcuts must not fire. */
12	const TYPING = ['INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'SELECT']
13	
14	/**
15	 * The deck's global keyboard, and the timer that drives the tour.
16	 *
17	 * `1`, `2` and `3` select a view and `Esc` clears the selected agent and the
18	 * selected finding, so each stage flies back on the one key whichever view is
19	 * up; `F` toggles the full-bleed stage and `P` the tour. Every other key, and any
20	 * press anywhere on the page, ends a running tour — a tour is what the deck
21	 * does while nobody is driving, so the first sign of a driver stops it.
22	 *
23	 * The step counter lives in the effect rather than in the route, so the cadence
24	 * stays at {@link TOUR_STEP_MS} whatever a navigation costs.
25	 */
26	export function usePresentation(): void {
27	  const router = useRouter()
28	  const pathname = usePathname()
29	  const presentation = useDeck(state => state.presentation)
30	  const setPresentation = useDeck(state => state.setPresentation)
31	  const togglePresentation = useDeck(state => state.togglePresentation)
32	  const selectAgent = useDeck(state => state.selectAgent)
33	  const selectFinding = useDeck(state => state.selectFinding)
34	
35	  const here = useRef(pathname)
36	  here.current = pathname
37	  const mode = useRef(presentation)
38	  mode.current = presentation
39	
40	  useEffect(() => {
41	    const leaveTour = (): void => {
42	      if (mode.current === 'tour') setPresentation('off')
43	    }
44	
45	    const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
46	      const target = event.target
47	      if (target instanceof HTMLElement && TYPING.includes(target.tagName)) return
48	      if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey) return
49	
50	      const key = event.key.toLowerCase()
51	      if (key === 'f') {
52	        togglePresentation('focus')
53	        return
54	      }
55	      if (key === 'p') {
56	        togglePresentation('tour')
57	        return
58	      }
59	
60	      leaveTour()
61	      if (event.key === 'Escape') {
62	        selectAgent(undefined)
63	        selectFinding(undefined)
64	        return
65	      }
66	      const view = VIEWS.find(entry => entry.key === event.key)
67	      if (view !== undefined) router.push(view.href)
68	    }
69	
70	    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
71	    window.addEventListener('pointerdown', leaveTour)
72	    return () => {
73	      window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
74	      window.removeEventListener('pointerdown', leaveTour)
75	    }
76	  }, [router, selectAgent, selectFinding, setPresentation, togglePresentation])
77	
78	  useEffect(() => {
79	    if (presentation !== 'tour') return
80	    // Start from whatever is on screen, so pressing P does not jump the view.
81	    let step = VIEWS.findIndex(entry => entry.href === here.current)
82	    const timer = setInterval(() => {
83	      step = (step + 1) % VIEWS.length
84	      const next = VIEWS[step]
85	      if (next !== undefined) router.push(next.href)
86	    }, TOUR_STEP_MS)
87	    return () => clearInterval(timer)
88	  }, [presentation, router])
89	}

1	// Interleaved A/B frame-cost probe over CDP: 90-frame windows, 5 rounds, SwiftShader.
2	// usage: node perf.mjs <urlA> <urlB> [rounds] [settleMs]
3	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
4	import { setTimeout as sleep } from 'node:timers/promises'
5	
6	const [, , urlA, urlB, roundsArg, settleArg] = process.argv
7	const rounds = Number(roundsArg ?? 5)
8	const settle = Number(settleArg ?? 9000)
9	const PORT = 9341
10	
11	const chrome = spawn('/opt/pw-browsers/chromium', [
12	  '--headless=new',
13	  '--no-sandbox',
14	  '--disable-dev-shm-usage',
15	  '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
16	  '--hide-scrollbars',
17	  '--force-device-scale-factor=1',
18	  '--window-size=900,600',
19	  `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`,
20	  'about:blank',
21	], { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] })
22	chrome.stderr.on('data', () => {})
23	
24	async function firstPage() {
25	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt++) {
26	    try {
27	      const list = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json()
28	      const page = list.find(t => t.type === 'page')
29	      if (page) return page
30	    } catch {}
31	    await sleep(400)
32	  }
33	  throw new Error('chromium devtools never came up')
34	}
35	
36	const page = await firstPage()
37	const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl)
38	await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
39	  ws.addEventListener('open', resolve, { once: true })
40	  ws.addEventListener('error', reject, { once: true })
41	})
42	
43	let nextId = 0
44	const pending = new Map()
45	const events = new Map()
46	ws.addEventListener('message', (message) => {
47	  const payload = JSON.parse(message.data)
48	  if (payload.id !== undefined) {
49	    const entry = pending.get(payload.id)
50	    pending.delete(payload.id)
51	    if (entry) entry.resolve(payload.result ?? payload.error)
52	    return
53	  }
54	  const waiters = events.get(payload.method) ?? []
55	  events.set(payload.method, [])
56	  for (const waiter of waiters) waiter(payload.params)
57	})
58	
59	function send(method, params = {}) {
60	  const id = ++nextId
61	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
62	    pending.set(id, { resolve })
63	    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))
64	  })
65	}
66	
67	function once(method, timeoutMs = 30000) {
68	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
69	    const list = events.get(method) ?? []
70	    list.push(resolve)
71	    events.set(method, list)
72	    setTimeout(() => resolve(undefined), timeoutMs)
73	  })
74	}
75	
76	await send('Page.enable')
77	await send('Runtime.enable')
78	await send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width: 900, height: 600, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false })
79	
80	const MEASURE = `(async () => {
81	  const frames = []
82	  await new Promise((resolve) => {
83	    let last = performance.now()
84	    let seen = 0
85	    const step = (now) => {
86	      frames.push(now - last)
87	      last = now
88	      seen += 1
89	      if (seen >= 90) { resolve(); return }
90	      requestAnimationFrame(step)
91	    }
92	    requestAnimationFrame((now) => { last = now; requestAnimationFrame(step) })
93	  })
94	  const sorted = [...frames].sort((a, b) => a - b)
95	  return JSON.stringify({
96	    median: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)],
97	    mean: frames.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / frames.length,
98	    p90: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length * 0.9)],
99	    n: frames.length,
100	  })
101	})()`
102	
103	async function measure(url) {
104	  const loaded = once('Page.loadEventFired')
105	  await send('Page.navigate', { url })
106	  await loaded
107	  await sleep(settle)
108	  const result = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression: MEASURE, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true })
109	  if (result?.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(result.exceptionDetails).slice(0, 300))
110	  return JSON.parse(result.result.value)
111	}
112	
113	const samples = { A: [], B: [] }
114	for (let round = 0; round < rounds; round++) {
115	  for (const [label, url] of [['A', urlA], ['B', urlB]]) {
116	    const sample = await measure(url)
117	    samples[label].push(sample.median)
118	    console.log(`round ${round + 1} ${label} median ${sample.median.toFixed(2)}ms mean ${sample.mean.toFixed(2)}ms p90 ${sample.p90.toFixed(2)}ms`)
119	  }
120	}
121	
122	const mid = list => [...list].sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor(list.length / 2)]
123	const a = mid(samples.A)
124	const b = mid(samples.B)
125	console.log(`\nA medians ${samples.A.map(v => v.toFixed(2)).join(' ')} -> ${a.toFixed(2)}ms (${(1000 / a).toFixed(1)} fps)`)
126	console.log(`B medians ${samples.B.map(v => v.toFixed(2)).join(' ')} -> ${b.toFixed(2)}ms (${(1000 / b).toFixed(1)} fps)`)
127	console.log(`ratio B/A ${(b / a).toFixed(3)}x`)
128	
129	ws.close()
130	chrome.kill('SIGKILL')
131	process.exit(0)

1	import { readRunEvents } from '@/deck/fixtures.server'
2	
3	/** The replay stream is written per request and never cached. */
4	export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
5	
6	/** Share of the recorded stream delivered immediately, as the history replay. */
7	const BACKFILL_SHARE = 0.55
8	
9	/** Delay between the paced frames that follow the backfill. */
10	const PACE_MS = 330
11	
12	/** Heartbeat interval once the recording is exhausted and the stream stays open. */
13	const HEARTBEAT_MS = 15_000
14	
15	/**
16	 * `GET /api/fixtures/runs/:id/events` — the replay mirror of the feed's
17	 * Server-Sent Events stream.
18	 *
19	 * It behaves like the live endpoint: history first, then frames as they
20	 * happen, then an open connection. Pacing the tail is what makes a keyless
21	 * demo look like a running enterprise rather than a static file.
22	 * @param _request - Unused; the route is keyed entirely on the path.
23	 * @param context - Next's route context carrying the run id.
24	 * @returns The event stream response.
25	 */
26	export function GET(_request: Request, context: { params: { id: string } }): Response {
27	  let events
28	  try {
29	    events = readRunEvents(context.params.id)
30	  } catch {
31	    // An id with no recorded stream is a missing fixture, not a server fault.
32	    return new Response('no recorded stream for this run', { status: 404 })
33	  }
34	
35	  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
36	  const backfill = Math.floor(events.length * BACKFILL_SHARE)
37	  let cursor = 0
38	  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
39	  let heartbeat: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | undefined
40	
41	  const stream = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
42	    start(controller) {
43	      const send = (payload: string): void => controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(payload))
44	
45	      for (; cursor < backfill; cursor++) {
46	        send(`data: ${JSON.stringify(events[cursor])}\n\n`)
47	      }
48	
49	      const tick = (): void => {
50	        const event = events[cursor]
51	        if (event === undefined) {
52	          heartbeat = setInterval(() => send(': keep-alive\n\n'), HEARTBEAT_MS)
53	          return
54	        }
55	        send(`data: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`)
56	        cursor += 1
57	        timer = setTimeout(tick, PACE_MS)
58	      }
59	
60	      timer = setTimeout(tick, PACE_MS)
61	    },
62	    cancel() {
63	      if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer)
64	      if (heartbeat !== undefined) clearInterval(heartbeat)
65	    },
66	  })
67	
68	  return new Response(stream, {
69	    headers: {
70	      'content-type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8',
71	      'cache-control': 'no-cache, no-transform',
72	      connection: 'keep-alive',
73	    },
74	  })

1	/**
2	 * Reads the committed fixtures from disk for the deck's replay routes.
3	 *
4	 * Server-only: the fixtures stay files rather than bundled imports so the
5	 * event streams can be replayed with pacing, and so a reviewer can read the
6	 * exact bytes the demo shows.
7	 */
8	
9	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
10	import { join, normalize } from 'node:path'
11	import type { RunEvent } from './contract.ts'
12	
13	/** Absolute path of the fixtures directory. */
14	const FIXTURES = join(process.cwd(), 'fixtures')
15	
16	/**
17	 * Read one fixture file, refusing any path that escapes the fixtures tree.
18	 *
19	 * The run and review ids reaching these routes come from a URL, so they are
20	 * untrusted input at a process boundary even though the deck itself only ever
21	 * sends ids it read from `runs.json`.
22	 * @param relative - Path under `fixtures/`.
23	 * @returns The file's contents.
24	 */
25	function readFixture(relative: string): string {
26	  const path = normalize(join(FIXTURES, relative))
27	  if (!path.startsWith(FIXTURES)) throw new Error('fixture path escapes the fixtures directory')
28	  return readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * One fixture read as JSON.
33	 * @param relative - Path under `fixtures/`.
34	 * @returns The parsed value.
35	 */
36	export function readFixtureJson<T>(relative: string): T {
37	  return JSON.parse(readFixture(relative)) as T
38	}
39	
40	/**
41	 * One run's recorded events.
42	 * @param runId - The run whose JSONL stream to read.
43	 * @returns Every recorded event, in sequence order.
44	 */
45	export function readRunEvents(runId: string): RunEvent[] {
46	  return readFixture(`events/${runId}.jsonl`)
47	    .split('\n')
48	    .filter(line => line.trim() !== '')

3	// exercised without starting a real review. Reads phase from a file so the
4	// phase can be flipped while the deck is watching.
5	//   0 = just started, every department pending, nothing released
6	//   1 = running, three departments released
7	//   2 = finished and certified (as the record actually ended)
8	//   3 = finished with the certificate withheld
9	import { createServer } from 'node:http'
10	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
11	
12	const UPSTREAM = 'http://localhost:4711'
13	const RUN = '2026-09-19-nodegoat-2'

15	const PHASE_FILE = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/wave2-safety/phase'
16	const RELEASED = new Set(['secrets', 'injection', 'access'])
17	
18	const headers = {
19	  'access-control-allow-origin': '*',
20	  'content-type': 'application/json',
21	  'cache-control': 'no-store',
22	}
23	
24	const recorded = readFileSync(EVENTS, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(line => line.trim() !== '')
25	
26	function phase() {
27	  try {
28	    return Number(readFileSync(PHASE_FILE, 'utf8').trim())
29	  } catch {
30	    return 0
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	const server = createServer(async (request, response) => {
35	  const url = new URL(request.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')
36	  const at = phase()
37	  try {
38	    if (url.pathname === `/runs/${RUN}/events`) {
39	      response.writeHead(200, {
40	        'access-control-allow-origin': '*',
41	        'content-type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8',
42	        'cache-control': 'no-cache, no-transform',
43	        connection: 'keep-alive',
44	      })
45	      let cursor = 0
46	      const pace = Number(process.env.PACE_MS ?? 120)
47	      const timer = setInterval(() => {
48	        if (cursor >= recorded.length) return
49	        response.write(`data: ${recorded[cursor]}\n\n`)
50	        cursor += 1
51	      }, pace)
52	      request.on('close', () => clearInterval(timer))
53	      return
54	    }
55	
56	    if (url.pathname === '/runs') {
57	      const runs = await (await fetch(`${UPSTREAM}/runs`)).json()
58	      const patched = runs.map(run => (run.id === RUN
59	        ? (at < 2
60	            ? { ...run, status: 'running', startedAt: new Date(Date.now() - 20_000).toISOString(), endedAt: undefined }
61	            : { ...run, status: 'completed', startedAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1_260_000).toISOString() })
62	        : run))
63	      // The deck follows the first code-safety run it is given.
64	      patched.sort((left, right) => (left.id === RUN ? -1 : right.id === RUN ? 1 : 0))
65	      response.writeHead(200, headers)
66	      response.end(JSON.stringify(patched))
67	      return
68	    }
69	
70	    if (url.pathname.startsWith('/safety/')) {
71	      const detail = await (await fetch(`${UPSTREAM}/safety/${RUN}`)).json()
72	      if (at >= 2) {
73	        const withheld = at === 3
74	        response.writeHead(200, headers)
75	        response.end(JSON.stringify(withheld
76	          ? {
77	              ...detail,
78	              departments: detail.departments.map((d, i) => (i > 3 ? { ...d, certified: false } : d)),
79	              certificate: {
80	                ...detail.certificate,
81	                verified: false,
82	                unverified: detail.findings.slice(0, 3).map(f => f.id),
83	              },
84	            }
85	          : detail))
86	        return
87	      }
88	      const released = at === 0 ? new Set() : RELEASED
89	      const findings = detail.findings.filter(f => released.has(String(f.id).split('-')[0]))
90	      const departments = detail.departments.map(department => (released.has(department.id)
91	        ? { ...department, certified: false }
92	        : { ...department, status: 'pending', certified: false, findings: 0 }))
93	      const counts = { critical: 0, high: 0, medium: 0, low: 0, info: 0 }
94	      for (const finding of findings) counts[finding.severity] += 1
95	      response.writeHead(200, headers)
96	      response.end(JSON.stringify({
97	        ...detail,
98	        findings,
99	        departments,
100	        certificate: { ...detail.certificate, verified: false, counts, unverified: [] },
101	      }))
102	      return
103	    }
104	
105	    const upstream = await fetch(`${UPSTREAM}${url.pathname}${url.search}`)
106	    response.writeHead(upstream.status, {
107	      ...headers,
108	      'content-type': upstream.headers.get('content-type') ?? 'application/json',
109	    })
110	    response.end(Buffer.from(await upstream.arrayBuffer()))
111	  } catch (error) {
112	    response.writeHead(500, headers)
113	    response.end(JSON.stringify({ error: String(error) }))
114	  }
115	})
116	
117	server.listen(4712, () => console.log('stage-feed on http://localhost:4712'))

input.content:
feat(deck): time the launch sequence and the verdict

Both set pieces are transitions, never states. The launch sequence plays for a review that starts while the deck is watching — every department pending, the run still running, started inside ninety seconds — and names the six departments with the charter each one's own opening directive states. The verdict plays when a review the deck has already seen unfinished reaches its certificate, in the words of the certificate itself: the departments that certified, the examiner it names, its severity counts, and what it leaves unverified.

A review loaded in its final state plays neither, and the run ids already played are held per module, so leaving the view or touring through it does not replay a moment.

input.content:
feat(deck): light the code city with the trail, the launch and the verdict

A building carries its read trail as one more instanced attribute: the acting department's colour and the scene time the file was opened at. The shader lights more of the tower's windows, runs a band of light up its walls and decays it, then holds a faint tint for the rest of the run, so nothing about the trail costs a frame that is not drawing it. The verdict ring travels out from the city centre and each beacon bursts as it reaches that beacon's own distance, which the beacons carry in the attribute they already had.

Under reduced motion the city holds a steady highlight on the last file touched alone, the launch sequence is one static card, and the verdict is the card without the ring or the burst.

The Safety view also reads a finished review once more on the refresh that first reports its run as no longer running, because the store stops re-reading a code-safety review at that point and would otherwise hold the last running snapshot and never see the certificate.

Frame cost on the Safety view under software rendering: 200.1 ms to 200.0 ms per frame, pooled over five interleaved ninety-frame windows — 1.00x, inside the noise of an A/A control on the same host.

content.text:
Everything is committed, gates pass, and my servers are stopped. Final report:

## Commits (oldest first, branch `worktree-agent-a8add07bf87d79a5d`, base `023d7c611`)

- `65373934e` feat(deck): resolve every tool event to the file it opened
- `037a6f138` feat(deck): time the launch sequence and the verdict
- `50b0cbb21` feat(deck): light the code city with the trail, the launch and the verdict

## Per-file summary

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/charters.ts` (new) | The six departments in start order: id, name, the one-line charter taken verbatim from each department's own opening directive in the run log, and its colour. `charterOfAgent` / `touchColor` map `code-safety-<dept>-integrator` to one of them; `code-safety-lead` falls to a neutral tint. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/read-trail.ts` (new) | The resolution and the fold. Indexes `safety.target.files` by basename, resolves one event through a `WeakMap` cache carried on the index, and folds `eventsUpTo(events, cursor)` into the most recent touch per file plus `opened` / `total` / `last`. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/FilesOpened.tsx` (new) | The panel-header counter. Subscribes to the store itself so the findings table does not re-render per event; drawn only while a department is pending. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/moments.ts` (new) | When each set piece plays, plus `useFinalRead` (see "Shared changes I need"). Module-level `launched` / `announced` / `seen` maps make each moment once-per-run-id across remounts and the tour. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/LaunchSequence.tsx` (new) | The 8 s overlay: target name, file count, six rows igniting at 820 ms intervals in their colours. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/VerdictCard.tsx` (new) | The 10 s card: kinetic CERTIFIED / NOT CERTIFIED, `n of m departments certified · k findings`, the examiner from `certificate.verifier` or the `certificate.unverified` list, and the five `certificate.counts`. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/moments.module.css` (new) | Both overlays' styling, including the `data-reduced` branches. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/SafetyStage.tsx` | `aFlare` (vec4: department colour + scene time) on the building geometry and the flare/pulse/mark in its shader; `aInfo` on beacons and halos widened to vec3 to carry each beacon's distance from the centre; `uFlare`/`uTime` on both beacon materials; `createVerdictMaterial` + `VerdictRing`; `useSceneStamp`; a `LiveCity` group that owns the trail subscription and the verdict stamp. |
| `apps/command-deck/components/safety/SafetyView.tsx` | Calls `useSafetyMoments`, passes `verdict` to the stage, mounts the two overlays inside `.stage`, and puts `<FilesOpened />` in the panel head. |

`deck/layout-city.ts` needed no change.

## How each moment starts and ends

**Read trail** — always on while the followed run has events. Every admitted `kind === 'tool'` event resolves to at most one inventory file; a new touch stamps `clock.elapsedTime` into `aFlare.w`, the shader decays `exp(-1.2·age)` (a twentieth at 2.5 s) and runs a band of light up the walls in 0.85 s, then the file holds a `0.13` mark of the department colour for the rest of the run. Scrubbing the timeline back removes touches and clears their flare. Reduced motion: `uSteady = 1` and only `trail.last` gets an attribute, so exactly one building holds a steady highlight.

**Launch sequence** — fires once per run id, on the first render where the review has loaded *and* the run is `running` *and* every department is `pending` *and* `startedAt` is inside 90 s. The run id is marked seen on that first render whether or not it qualifies, so a review that loads later never triggers it. A `veil` animation fades the overlay out at 8 s and a timer unmounts it.

**Verdict** — `seen` records `{verified, ended}` on the first render per run id without firing. A later change to `verified === true` plays `certified`; a change to "no department pending, still unverified" plays `uncertified`. A review that loads already finished sets `seen` and never transitions. The card fades out at 10 s; the ring travels for 3.2 s from the city centre and each beacon bursts when the ring reaches its own radius. Reduced motion: card only, no ring, no burst (`useSceneStamp` is passed `undefined`).

## The resolution rule and its misses

Take the `<path>…</path>` values when the detail has any, otherwise every absolute token (`/[\w.][\w./+-]*`); for each, keep the longest inventory path `p` with `token === p || token.endsWith('/' + p)`; cache per event object on the index.

Measured on the committed `2026-09-19-nodegoat-2` stream (1,079 events, 634 tool events, 317 of them carrying a `detail`): **124 resolve, covering 51 of 111 inventory files** — 103 `read`, 15 `grep`, 6 `bash`; all six departments contribute (secrets 31, data 29, platform 24, injection 21, access 16, dependencies 3). So the counter tops out near "51 of 111", as you predicted.

Misses, all by design: the request half of each tool pair carries no `detail`; a department's own worktree files (`REPORTING.md`, `findings/*.json`, skill text) are correct non-matches; a `grep` result naming ten inventory files flares only the longest match, so the other nine are counted only when some later event names them; a basename that matches but whose parent directories do not align on a `/` is rejected; `finding` and `certificate` events are not part of the trail even when they name a file.

## Frame cost

Headless Chromium, SwiftShader, 900×600, replay mode (`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` unreachable so the fixture stream paces itself identically in both arms), two production builds served side by side, 5 interleaved rounds with the A/B order alternating, 90-frame windows with the first 15 frames dropped.

- A/A control on the baseline build: pooled 150.0 ms vs 166.6 ms, **median per-round ratio 1.000×** — that is the noise floor of this host.
- Before (`023d7c611`, port 3211) pooled median **200.1 ms** (5.0 fps) over 375 frames.
- After (this branch, port 3212) pooled median **200.0 ms** (5.0 fps) over 375 frames.
- **Pooled ratio 1.000×; median per-round ratio 0.923×.** Budget was ≤ 1.5×.

## README sentences you can paste

> While a review runs, every file a department opens flares on its own building in that department's colour and fades over about two and a half seconds, with a short pulse running up the tower; the file then keeps a faint tint of that colour, so the city fills in as the review reads it and the panel counts `N of 111 files opened` from the same resolution. A review that starts while the deck is watching opens on an eight-second launch sequence in which the six departments ignite one after another with what each one reads the code for. A review that reaches its certificate while the deck is watching plays a ten-second verdict — CERTIFIED or NOT CERTIFIED, the departments that certified, the examiner the certificate names and its severity counts — over a ground ring that travels out from the city centre and bursts each beacon as it passes; a review loaded in its final state plays neither, because nothing happened while anyone was watching. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the city holds a steady highlight on the last file touched alone, the launch sequence is one static card, and the verdict is the card without the ring or the burst.

## Shared changes I need

1. **`apps/command-deck/deck/store.ts`, `refresh()`** — the condition `selected.status === 'running' || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id` stops re-reading a code-safety review the moment the feed stops calling the run `running`. The last detail read is therefore up to one 10 s refresh older than the certificate the examiner writes at the end, so the deck can hold a finished review's running snapshot indefinitely and never see the verdict — I reproduced exactly that before working around it. It should also re-read once on the transition away from `running`. My local workaround is `useFinalRead` in `components/safety/moments.ts`, which calls `useDeck.getState().loadSafety(id, true)` once; delete it when the store owns this.

2. **`apps/command-deck/deck/palette.ts`** — there is no department colour anywhere. I wrote the six out in `components/safety/charters.ts` as `divisionColor('code-safety')` rotated across the same 84° band `deck/pipeline.ts` gives lanes that share a division (secrets `#ff5ff6` → platform `#ffa85f`). Please export `departmentColor(id)` from `deck/palette.ts`, make `deck/pipeline.ts`'s lane spread and `charters.ts` both read it, and the process lanes and the city's read trail will be the same colour by construction instead of by hand. Note the two warmest of the six sit close to the `high` and `medium` severity hues; if that bothers you in the room, that one exported function is the place to shift the band.

3. **Docs** — `apps/command-deck/docs/safety.png` no longer matches: a loaded review now shows the read marks of the files it opened. Retake it when you integrate docs.
